ety.text: From earlier tattaow, tattow, a borrowing from a Polynesian language, e.g. Samoan tatau (“tattoo; to tap, to strike”).
From earlier tap-to, borrowed from Dutch taptoe, from tap (“tap; faucet on a cask”) + toe (“to; shut”). More at tap, to.

senses.d: An image made on a body part, usually the skin with ink and a needle.
ex: His shirt sleeves were turned up, so upon his brawny arms his tattooes were visible.

senses.d: A method of decorating a body part, usually the skin, by inserting colored substances under the surface with a sharp instrument (usually a solenoid-driven needle).
To apply a tattoo to (someone or something).
ex: She made Silas tattoo an anchor on her arm like his

senses.d: To hit the ball hard, as if to figuratively leave a tattoo on the ball.
ex: Jones tattoos one into the gap in left; that will clear the bases.

senses.d: A signal played five minutes before taps (lights out).
ex: Study goes on until tattoo, which, when Pops was at the Point, was sounded at 9.30, followed by taps at 10.

senses.d: A signal by drum or bugle ordering soldiers to return to their quarters.

ex: the right hand became restless and began to beat out a silent tattoo upon the tabletop

senses.d: To tap rhythmically on, to drum.
A pony of a certain breed from India.

grp.label: an image made in the skin with ink and a needle
